verses.text: These are the priests and Levites who came back with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and with Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,
Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,
Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah. These were the leaders of the priests and their relatives in the time of Jeshua.
The Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. Mattaniah and his relatives were in charge of the songs of thanks.
Bakbukiah and Unno, their relatives, stood across from them during the services.
Jeshua was the father of Joiakim. Joiakim was the father of Eliashib. Eliashib was the father of Joiada.
Joiada was the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan was the father of Jaddua.
In the time of Joiakim, these priests were the family leaders: from Seraiah's family, Meraiah; from Jeremiah's, Hananiah;
from Ezra's, Meshullam; from Amariah's, Jehohanan;
from Malluchi's, Jonathan; from Shebaniah's, Joseph;
from Harim's, Adna; from Meraioth's, Helkai;
from Iddo's, Zechariah; from Ginnethon's, Meshullam;
from Abijah's, Zichri; from Miniamin's and Moadiah's, Piltai;
from Bilgah's, Shammua; from Shemaiah's, Jehonathan;
from Joiarib's, Mattenai; from Jedaiah's, Uzzi;
from Sallai's, Kallai; from Amok's, Eber;
from Hilkiah's, Hashabiah; and from Jedaiah's, Nethanel.
In the time of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, the family leaders of the Levites and the priests were written down, while Darius the Persian was king.
The family leaders of the Levites were written in the book of the records up to the time of Johanan son of Eliashib.

The leaders of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua son of Kadmiel. Their relatives stood across from them to praise and give thanks, one group answering the other, as David the man of God had commanded.
Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers who guarded the storerooms at the gates.
They served in the time of Joiakim son of Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and in the time of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and teacher.

When the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated, the Levites were brought in from wherever they lived to Jerusalem. They came to celebrate the dedication with joy, with songs of thanks, and with cymbals, harps, and lyres.
The singers also gathered from the area around Jerusalem, from the villages of the Netophathites,
from Beth Gilgal, and from the area of Geba and Azmaveth. The singers had built villages for themselves around Jerusalem.
The priests and Levites made themselves clean, and then they made the people, the gates, and the wall clean.
I had the leaders of Judah go up on top of the wall. I also chose two large choirs to give thanks and march along the wall. One choir went to the right, toward the Garbage Gate.
Hoshaiah and half of the leaders of Judah followed them,
along with Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,
Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah.
Some of the priests also followed with trumpets, along with Zechariah son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph,
and his relatives Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani. They played the musical instruments of David the man of God. Ezra the teacher led this group.
At the Fountain Gate they went straight up the steps of the City of David, on the slope of the wall, above David's palace, to the Water Gate on the east.
The second choir went the other way, to the left. I followed them on top of the wall, together with half the people. We went past the Tower of the Ovens to the Broad Wall,
over the Ephraim Gate, the Old Gate, the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel, and the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Sheep Gate. We stopped at the Gate of the Guard.
Then the two choirs that gave thanks took their places in God's temple. So did I, together with half of the officials,
and the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with their trumpets,
and also Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. The singers sang loudly, led by Jezrahiah.
That day they offered many sacrifices and celebrated, because God had given them great joy. The women and children also celebrated. The sound of joy in Jerusalem could be heard far away.

On that day men were chosen to be in charge of the storerooms for the gifts, the first part of the harvest, and the tenths. From the fields around the towns, they were to bring into the storerooms the shares the law required for the priests and Levites. The people of Judah were happy with the priests and Levites who served.
They did the work of their God and the work of making things clean, as did the singers and gatekeepers, as David and his son Solomon had commanded.
Long ago, in the time of David and Asaph, there were leaders of the singers, and songs of praise and thanks to God.

So in the time of Zerubbabel and of Nehemiah, all Israel gave daily shares for the singers and gatekeepers. They also set apart a share for the other Levites, and the Levites set apart a share for the priests, the descendants of Aaron.
